info.title: anony-mail API
info.summary: REST + Server-Sent Events API for an inbound-only disposable email backend.
info.description:
anony-mail is an inbound-only disposable email (temp mail) backend. It receives mail over SMTP for throwaway addresses and exposes it through this HTTP API. It does **not** send mail.

### Conventions
- **Base path:** every resource endpoint lives under `/api`; the health check is at `/healthz`.
- **Content type:** request and response bodies are JSON, except attachment downloads (raw bytes) and the events endpoint (an SSE stream).
- **Addresses are case-insensitive.** They are lowercased server-side before lookup or creation, so `Foo@Example.com` and `foo@example.com` refer to the same mailbox.
- **Timestamps** are UTC in RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 format (e.g. `2026-07-01T11:23:45.123456Z`).
- **IDs** (message and attachment) are UUIDs (v4).

### Errors
On failure the API returns the matching HTTP status code with a JSON body of the form `{ "error": "message" }`. A `500` always reports a generic `"internal server error"` message; details are logged server-side.

### Authentication (owner tokens)
Reads are open by design (temp mail is semi-public): anyone who knows an address can fetch the mailbox, its messages, attachments, and the SSE stream. **Destructive and lifecycle operations are gated by an owner token**: creating an address returns a one-time `owner_token` (`am_` + 43 base64url chars). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <owner_token>` for extend, rotate, mailbox delete, and message delete; requests without a valid token fail with `401` and a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header. The token is never returned again — store it client-side. Losing it means losing control of the mailbox (it stays readable until it expires). `POST /api/addresses/{address}/rotate` reissues the token and instantly revokes the old one.

### Rate limiting
Requests are rate limited per client IP (general bucket plus a stricter one on address creation, and a daily per-IP address-creation quota). Exceeding a limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`.

### Mailbox lifecycle
Mailboxes expire after `DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 1 hour) and are periodically purged along with their messages and attachments. Use `POST /api/addresses/{address}/extend` to push the expiry back.

get.description: Simple liveness probe. Always returns `200` with `{ "status": "ok" }` when the HTTP server is up. Never touches the database — use `/readyz` for readiness.

Readiness probe: verifies the storage backend answers a trivial query (`SELECT 1` on SQL backends). Returns `200` with `{ "status": "ready" }` when the service can do useful work, `503` when the database is unreachable — point load-balancer/orchestrator readiness probes here.

200.description: The service is ready to serve traffic.

get.description: Returns the domains this server accepts mail for (the `DOMAINS` setting). The first entry is the default used when creating an address without specifying a domain.

post.description:
Creates a new mailbox and returns it **together with its one-time `owner_token`** — store the token client-side; it is required for extend, rotate, and all delete operations and is never returned again. The request body is **optional**:

- Omit the body entirely (or send `{}`) to get a random 10-character local part on the first configured domain.
- Provide `domain` to choose among the configured domains.
- Provide `local_part` to request a custom address. It must be 1–64 characters of `[a-z0-9._-]` and must not start or end with a separator (`.`, `_`, `-`). If the address is already taken, the request fails with `409 Conflict`.

Reserved role/validation local parts (`admin`, `postmaster`, `webmaster`, `abuse`, `ssladmin`, ... — RFC 2142 plus the CA/Browser-Forum set, extensible server-side via `RESERVED_LOCAL_PARTS`) cannot be claimed and fail with `400 Bad Request`.

Creation is rate limited per IP (including a daily quota); exceeding it fails with `429 Too Many Requests`.

The new mailbox expires after the server's default TTL (`DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS`, 1 hour by default).

random.summary: Random address on the default domain (empty body)

domainOnly.summary: Random local part on a chosen domain

custom.summary: Custom local part on a chosen domain

201.description: Mailbox created. The `owner_token` appears **only** in this response (and in a rotate response); it cannot be recovered later.

409.description: The requested custom address already exists.

get.description: Returns the mailbox's metadata if it exists. Note that an expired-but-not-yet-purged mailbox is still returned here; compare `expires_at` against the current time to determine whether it is still active.

delete.description: Deletes the mailbox and all of its messages and attachments (cascading). Requires the owner token. Returns `204 No Content` on success.

post.description: Pushes the mailbox's `expires_at` to now + the server default TTL (`DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS`). The extension is relative to the current time, not to the previous expiry. Requires the owner token (which stays the same — extending never rotates it). No request body is required.

200.description: Expiry extended; the updated mailbox is returned.

post.description: Reissues the mailbox's owner token and returns the new one; the previous token is revoked **immediately**. Use this if the token may have leaked. Requires the current owner token. No request body is required.

200.description: Token rotated. This response is the only place the new token appears.

get.description:
Returns lightweight summaries of the mailbox's messages, newest first (ordered by `received_at` then `id`, both descending). Bodies and attachment metadata are omitted here — fetch a single message for the full content. An existing mailbox with no mail returns `200` with an empty array `[]`; a missing mailbox returns `404`.

Pagination: `limit` caps the page size (default 50, max 200). `since` is a keyset cursor — pass the id of the newest message you have seen and only strictly newer messages are returned, which is the cheap way to poll for deltas (e.g. after a push notification). If the `since` message no longer exists (expired, deleted, or dropped by quota), the cursor is ignored and the newest page is returned.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of summaries to return. Values above 200 are clamped.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Keyset cursor: return only messages strictly newer than this message id.

delete.summary: Delete all messages in a mailbox
delete.description: Deletes every message (and their attachments) in the mailbox in one call. The mailbox itself, its expiry, and its owner token are untouched. Requires the owner token.

get.description:
Returns a single message including its text and/or HTML bodies and attachment metadata. Attachment bytes are not inlined — download them individually via the attachments endpoint using each attachment's `id`.

Security note: `html_body` is untrusted, attacker-controlled markup (anyone can email the inbox). Render it only in a sandboxed iframe or after sanitization — see the schema description.

value.subject: Invoice #1042
value.text_body: Thanks for your order. Your invoice is attached.
value.html_body: Thanks for your order. Your invoice is attached.

value.subject: Your verification code
value.text_body: Your verification code is 123456. It expires in 10 minutes.

delete.description: Deletes one message (and its attachments) from the mailbox. Requires the owner token. Returns `204 No Content` on success.

post.description: Sets the message's `seen` flag. Idempotent — marking an already-read message succeeds. Open like the read endpoints (knowing the address already grants read access), so no owner token is required.

get.description: Returns the message's original RFC 5322 bytes as received over SMTP (dot-unstuffed), served as `message/rfc822` with an attachment disposition (`{id}.eml`) and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Only available when the server runs with `STORE_RAW_MESSAGE=true`; otherwise — and for messages delivered before the toggle was enabled — this endpoint returns `404`.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment disposition named after the message id.

404.description: Message not found, or raw retention is disabled.

example.error: raw message not available (missing, or raw retention is disabled)

get.description: Streams the raw bytes of an attachment. The response's `Content-Type` is the attachment's stored MIME type, except that browser-active types (`text/html`, `application/xhtml+xml`, `image/svg+xml`, `text/xml`, `application/xml`) are served as `application/octet-stream` so a crafted attachment cannot execute on the API origin — the real type remains available in the message's attachment metadata. Every response carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. `Content-Disposition` is set to `attachment` with a sanitized ASCII filename, plus an RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''…` form when the original name is non-ASCII.

Content-Type.description: The attachment's stored MIME type, e.g. `application/pdf`. Browser-active types are replaced with `application/octet-stream`.

Content-Disposition.description: Download disposition with a sanitized ASCII filename, plus an RFC 5987 `filename*` form for non-ASCII names.

X-Content-Type-Options.description: Always `nosniff`: forbids MIME sniffing of the download.

404.description: The attachment (or its message/mailbox) was not found.

get.description: Reports which push channels this server can deliver on: `webpush` (browsers/PWAs via VAPID) and `apns` (native iOS apps). Use it to decide whether to prompt the user for notification permission at all.
Returns the server's VAPID public key. Pass it (decoded from base64url) as `applicationServerKey` to `PushManager.subscribe` in the browser.

post.summary: Register a push subscription (Web Push or APNs)
post.description:
Registers a push subscription for this mailbox so new-mail notifications reach the device. Requires the owner token. Two shapes share this endpoint:

- **Web Push** (browser/PWA): send `PushSubscription.toJSON()`, i.e. `{ endpoint, keys: { p256dh, auth } }`.
- **APNs** (native iOS app): send `{ device_token }` — the hex token from `didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken`.

The `kind` field is optional; it is inferred from which identifier is present. Subscribing to a channel the server has no credentials for answers `503` (check `GET /api/push/config` first). Idempotent per `(mailbox, endpoint/token)`: re-subscribing refreshes the record instead of creating a duplicate. The number of subscriptions per mailbox (all kinds combined) is capped server-side (`MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_MAILBOX`, default 5).

requestBody.description: A Web Push subscription or an APNs device token.

delete.description: Unregisters the subscription identified by its Web Push `endpoint` or APNs `device_token` (provide either). Requires the owner token. Works even when the server currently has no push credentials, so clients can always clean up.

404.description: The mailbox or subscription was not found.

200.description: An open `text/event-stream`. Each `message` event carries a JSON `MailEvent` in its `data` field.

schema.description:
SSE-framed stream. Each record is `event: message
data: <MailEvent JSON>

`. See the MailEvent schema for the data shape.

ownerToken.description: Per-mailbox owner token returned once by `POST /api/addresses` (and by rotate). Format: `am_` + 43 base64url characters. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <owner_token>`.

AddressPath.name: address
AddressPath.description: Full email address of the mailbox. Case-insensitive (lowercased server-side). The `@` may be sent literally or percent-encoded as `%40`.

BadRequest.description: The request was invalid (e.g. unknown domain or malformed `local_part`).

unknownDomain.summary: Domain is not in the server's DOMAINS list

value.error: local_part must be 1-64 chars of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' or '-' and not start/end with a separator

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid owner token. The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.

TooManyRequests.description: A per-IP rate limit or quota was exceeded. Retry later.

PushNotConfigured.description: The server has no credentials for the requested push channel (no VAPID keypair for `webpush`, no APNs key for `apns`). Check `GET /api/push/config`.

MailboxNotFound.description: No mailbox exists for this address.

MessageNotFound.description: No such message in this mailbox.

InternalError.description: An unexpected server error occurred. Details are logged server-side.

CreateAddressRequest.description: Options for creating a mailbox. Every field is optional; an empty object (or no body) yields a random address on the first configured domain. Unknown fields are ignored.

local_part.description: Custom local part (the portion before `@`). Must be 1–64 characters of `[a-z0-9._-]` and must not start or end with a separator (`.`, `_`, `-`). Lowercased before use. If omitted, a random 10-character local part is generated.

domain.description: One of the server's configured domains (see `GET /api/domains`). Defaults to the first configured domain when omitted.

CreateAddressResponse.description: A newly created mailbox plus its one-time owner token.

owner_token.description: Bearer token proving ownership of this mailbox (`am_` + 43 base64url chars). Returned **only** here and from rotate — store it; it cannot be recovered. Required for extend, rotate, and all deletes.

RotateTokenResponse.description: The replacement owner token issued by a rotate; the previous token is already revoked.

owner_token.description: The new owner token. Same format and handling rules as at creation.

address.description: Full email address of the mailbox (lowercased).

expires_at.description: When the mailbox expires and becomes eligible for purging (UTC).

deleted.description: Number of messages that were deleted.

MessageSummary.description: Lightweight message representation used in inbox listings (no bodies or attachment metadata).

mail_from.description: SMTP envelope sender (MAIL FROM) of the message.

subject.description: Message subject, or null if the email had no Subject header.

received_at.description: When the server received and stored the message (UTC).

has_attachments.description: True if the message has one or more attachments.

seen.description: True once the message was marked read via the read endpoint.

AttachmentMeta.description: Attachment metadata returned alongside a full message. Download the bytes via the attachment endpoint.

id.description: Attachment identifier; use it in the download URL.

filename.description: Original filename, or null if the part had none.

content_type.description: MIME type of the attachment as parsed from the message.

size.description: Size of the attachment content in bytes.

StoredMessage.description: A fully materialised message including bodies and attachment metadata.

mailbox_address.description: Address of the mailbox this message belongs to.

mail_from.description: SMTP envelope sender (MAIL FROM) of the message.

subject.description: Message subject, or null if absent.

message_date.description: Date parsed from the message's Date header (UTC), or null if missing/unparseable.

text_body.description: Plain-text body, or null if the message had none.
examples: Thanks for your order. Your invoice is attached.

html_body.description: HTML body, or null if the message had none. UNTRUSTED, attacker-controlled markup: anyone can email this mailbox, and the server stores and returns the HTML verbatim. Never inject it into a live DOM — render it inside a sandboxed iframe (`<iframe sandbox>` without `allow-scripts`) or sanitize it first (e.g. DOMPurify), and block remote content by default.
examples: Thanks for your order. Your invoice is attached.

raw_size.description: Size in bytes of the raw message as received over SMTP (DATA phase).

received_at.description: When the server received and stored the message (UTC).

seen.description: True once the message was marked read via the read endpoint.

attachments.description: Attachment metadata (bytes downloaded separately). Empty when there are none.

MailEvent.description: Payload delivered in the `data` field of each SSE `message` event. Mirrors a MessageSummary plus the target `address` and the server-extracted verification code, giving enough to render an inbox row immediately; treat the REST listing as authoritative.

address.description: The mailbox address the message arrived for.

id.description: Identifier of the newly stored message.

mail_from.description: SMTP envelope sender (MAIL FROM) of the message.

subject.description: Message subject, or null if absent.

received_at.description: When the server received and stored the message (UTC).

has_attachments.description: True if the message has one or more attachments.

code.description: OTP / verification code the server extracted from the subject or text body, or null if none was detected. Normalized to bare digits for numeric codes (e.g. `G-482913` becomes `482913`).

VapidPublicKeyResponse.description: The server's VAPID public key for `PushManager.subscribe`.

PushConfigResponse.description: Which push channels this server can deliver on.

webpush.description: True when a VAPID keypair is configured (browsers/PWAs).

apns.description: True when APNs credentials are configured (native iOS apps).

SubscriptionKind.description: Push channel: `webpush` (W3C Web Push with VAPID) or `apns` (Apple Push Notification service).

SubscribeRequest.description: A push subscription of either kind. Web Push: `{ endpoint, keys }`, exactly as produced by `PushSubscription.toJSON()`. APNs: `{ device_token }`. `kind` is optional and inferred from which identifier is present.

endpoint.description: Web Push only: HTTPS push-service URL unique to this device/browser.

device_token.description: APNs only: the hex device token from `didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken`.

SubscribeResponse.description: Confirmation of a registered push subscription.

id.description: Server-side id of the subscription (stable across re-subscribes of the same endpoint/token).

UnsubscribeRequest.description: Identifies the subscription to remove: provide the Web Push `endpoint` or the APNs `device_token`.

endpoint.description: The push-service URL used at registration (Web Push).

device_token.description: The device token used at registration (APNs).

DomainsResponse.description: The set of domains the server accepts mail for.

domains.description: Configured domains; the first is the default for address creation.

status.description: Always `"ok"` when the server is healthy.
Always `"ready"` when the storage backend answers queries.

Error.description: Uniform error envelope returned on any non-2xx response.
